services.name: Hearing test at home
services.story: The main story: a $179 hearing test at Pine Hill care home. Nothing is taken. The clinic bills Alex's plan its own way.

services.name: Hearing test at home
services.story: The same hearing test, paid privately: nothing is taken, and Rosie texts the $179 bill when Victor texts DONE.

services.name: Hearing aid repair at home
services.story: A hearing aid that stopped working, at the care home. Only the $89 home check is promised. Victor prices the repair at the visit, with Alex's yes first, and Rosie texts the bill.

services.name: Hearing aids fitted at home (a pair)
services.story: Hearing aids fitted at Pine Hill: $2,800 a pair, a $500 deposit when booked on the secure page, and Rosie texts the bill for the $2,300 rest when Victor texts DONE.

services_shape: visit types with a person, each with a set length; a hearing test needs the clinic's one sound booth, so two tests never overlap; hearing aids are chosen after a test, ordered, then fitted at a second visit about 2 weeks later, with follow-up adjustments during the trial
questions_before_times: for you, your child, or someone you help (a care home resident)
which visit: a hearing test, a free screening, a hearing aid check or repair, or earwax removal (the clinic's own visit types; never symptoms typed into the AI)
do you wear hearing aids now
a health plan (its name only), or paying yourself
the best way to reach you: texts, email, or a relay or captioned call
safety_stop: hearing that dropped suddenly, in one or both ears, over a few days or less (with or without new ringing or fullness)
ear pain with fluid, pus or blood coming from the ear, or ear pain with a high fever
dizziness or spinning that started suddenly, or ringing in one ear that started suddenly
a face that droops, weakness on one side, trouble speaking, or a hard blow to the head
first_steps: Health history, consent and the plan's papers
A doctor's order, where the plan asks for one
A written price estimate for self-pay patients
A doctor's OK before hearing aids, where the rules require one
license: always: each audiologist holds their own active license from the state's board; anyone who fits and sells prescription hearing aids holds the state's hearing aid license or registration (a switch from the state form)
staff_skills: audiologists: full hearing tests, children's tests, earwax removal, fittings, adjustments, repairs and results; hearing aid specialists: fittings, adjustments, cleanings and repairs, and the tests the state's rules let them run to fit aids (a switch); only people cleared for visits away go to care homes and homes
messages_never: texts carry only the clinic's name, the date, the time, the address and a secure link: never the visit type, the plan, the reason, results or medicines; at the clinic, not the audiologist's name either; when the audiologist or hearing aid specialist comes to a care home or home, their name stays, for the door check; a READY text says only that the order is in
demo_note: Demo data for testing only. [G] = prefilled from the business's Google listing at sign-up; the owner checks each field.
